Maintaining the 5.25–5.5% federal funds target and continuing balance-sheet runoff (QT) reflects a Taylor-rule-consistent response to elevated inflation, consistent with Clarida–Galí–Gertler’s empirical policy-rule framework and the Barro–Gordon emphasis on commitment to avoid inflation bias, supported by central bank independence (Bernanke). The statement’s attention to transmission lags and tighter credit conditions aligns with evidence that higher policy rates restrain bank lending and investment via the interest-rate and credit channels and with Romer & Romer’s identification of contractionary policy shocks’ real effects. While current activity is “solid” and the banking system “sound,” the recognition that restrictive policy will weigh on growth and hiring tempers the outlook. Overall tone: cautiously positive on present conditions but guarded about the forward path.
